title: Pre-existing cancellation did not prevent process launch

significance.impact: A provider process can begin despite cancellation already being set before the runner is entered.
significance.exposure: Every caller of the shared process runner that supplies an already-set cancellation event; provider startup can precede the later polling check.
significance.detectability: The caller may receive a later cancellation result even though the process was launched; the result alone does not expose that ordering.
significance.systemic_implication: The pre-launch cancellation control was missing from the shared provider-neutral boundary. Approval-wait, supervisor dispatch, teardown, and sibling input modes require distinct ordering checks rather than assuming cancellation reverses prior activity.
significance.recovery: A pre-spawn check prevents this condition prospectively. Actions that already began require native result inspection; cancellation cannot undo them.
significance.rationale: A missing cancellation ordering control in a shared side-effect boundary has broader reach than the immediate duplex feature. Local containment does not establish end-to-end cancellation integrity.

confidence.basis: The pre-fix boundary test reached a forbidden Popen call with cancellation set before run_bounded entry; the source places its original cancellation check after spawn.

evidence.observation: The selected test failed at the planted process-spawn assertion, not during collection or fixture setup.

claim.failure_mode: The first cancellation check occurred inside the process-polling loop after subprocess creation.
claim.downstream_consequence: An already-cancelled task could still start provider work or an authorized side effect before the runner terminates it.

counterevidence.observation: The existing active-process loop did observe cancellation and terminate the owned process group; the demonstrated gap is before launch, not absence of every cancellation control.

proof_limits: No live provider side effect was induced; the deterministic launch-boundary test establishes the missing ordering control.
The new pre-entry check is not an atomic cancellation-versus-spawn lock, native tool-action rollback, or full supervisor/approval-state proof.

containment: A pre-existing cancellation event now raises ProcessCancelled before subprocess creation.

remediation.description: Check cancellation before process creation and retain a permanent no-spawn regression.

evidence.observation: The cancellation check now precedes Popen; test_already_cancelled_request_never_reaches_spawn rejects reaching that boundary.

remediation.description: Qualify supervisor dispatch, native approval waiting/delivery, cancellation races, and installed recovery without treating queued input as acknowledged native execution.

required: The pre-entry no-spawn assertion must reject the original missing check.

Systemically challenge cancellation before dispatch, while awaiting native approval, concurrently with decision delivery, and during provider teardown; inspect exact native actions rather than only final state labels.
